title: Depth-five circuits for iterated matrix multiplication
author: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
description: An exposition of OpenAI's proof (2026) that every syntactically homogeneous arithmetic circuit with five alternating layers of sums and products that computes the (1,1) entry of a product of n matrices of size n x n, over a field of characteristic zero, has at least n^(sqrt(n)/400) gates for all large n; a circuit of size n^(sqrt(n)+4) exists over every field. The theorem is proved in full, with no hypothesis from the literature. The first lesson defines the polynomial and the circuits, describes what a homogeneous circuit computes, and proves the upper bound. The second lesson defines the rank measure: the variables of some layers are replaced by partial derivatives, the others by multiplications, and the rank of the resulting map between spaces of polynomials is taken; it proves that the rank of a product is small unless the degrees of the factors fit a fixed proportion. The third lesson proves that a circuit of size S has rank measure at most 2 S^2 D exp(11 sqrt n) n^(-sqrt(n)/100), where D is the dimension of the source space. The fourth lesson treats iterated matrix multiplication: two traces bound the rank from below; the first is a sum over paths, the second a sum over quadruples of paths, which is reduced to a sum over words in two letters. The fifth lesson bounds that sum, obtains rank at least D exp(-6 sqrt n), and proves the theorem over the complex numbers and over every field of characteristic zero.
prerequisites: core course Linear Algebra (B40): rank, trace, adjoint, orthogonal projection, determinants
polynomials in several variables, binomial coefficients, power series
the lessons prove every other fact they use; there is no named hypothesis

checks.reading: The manuscript 'Homogeneous depth-five lower bounds for iterated matrix multiplication' (OpenAI, 25 Sep 2026, in the revision of the repository on 13 Oct 2026; six sections, one figure, about 1,480 lines of TeX) was read in full on 13 Oct 2026, and every step of its argument was derived again while the lessons were written: the operators Q(d_V, U) and the rank measure; the parameter lemma; the product lemma with the intermediate spaces and the numbers H_e; the degree estimates and the sum of the corrections for even degrees; the bound for a circuit, with the expansion of one factor of large degree; the orthonormal monomial bases and the two traces; the occupation moments of a random composition and the comparison with geometric variables; the first trace; the formula with four paths, the two types of a layer, the tables of local polynomials and weights; the relaxation and the count for a type word; the removal of isolated positions; the discrepancy of the balanced division of the layers; the sum over runs; the comparison of the two bounds; the transfer to fields of characteristic zero; the block construction. No error found. Differences of presentation, none a correction: all constants are explicit (the corrections for even degrees add up to at most sqrt(n); the bound for a circuit has exp(11 sqrt n); the first trace loses at most exp(-6/sqrt n); the sum over type words is at most exp(3 sqrt n); the measure of IMM is at least D exp(-6 sqrt n)); the inequality rank >= T^2/T_2 is proved with the orthogonal projection onto the image and the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality for the trace inner product, without eigenvalues; the relaxed classes of quadruples, their count and the independence of the coincidence events are stated as separate lemmas. Own addition: with these constants the bound n^(sqrt(n)/400) follows for log n >= 3401 (n has 1478 digits), and the inequality obtained for the size is below 1 while log n <= 1700; the manuscript states the theorem with an unspecified n_0. The other conditions 'for large n' of the lessons are not computed explicitly; the largest one that is explicit in the text is n^(3/40) >= 5 (n >= 2.1 * 10^9). Checked by the program plan/checks_20261013/d5_check.py (nine parts: the parameter lemma with 60 digits for n = 10^4 to 10^8; the bounds for H_e; the ratios of dimensions; the product bound against exact ranks over the rationals on small examples; the moments of compositions; for small matrix products the map F_f in the normalized bases, both traces against the path formulas, the tables of local polynomials, the count n^(2L-w) and the probabilities n^(-h_t); the sum over type words computed exactly for n = 10^3, 10^4, 10^5 (logarithms 7.0, 14.3, 32.1, far below 3 sqrt n) with the discrepancy bound; the count of the block construction for n < 4000; the explicit constants at n = 10^10, 10^12 + 1, 10^14 and the threshold). All parts pass (output in d5_check_run_20261013.txt). Three earlier runs stopped because of faults of the check program itself: twice double precision was used where the bounds are of size 1e-17 or the integers have 20 digits, and once an assertion compared numbers of size e^1700 with 60 digits. They were corrected in the program; no statement of the lessons was changed. The account of earlier work in Section 1 of the manuscript was not checked and is not reproduced in the lessons.
checks.layout: Measured on 13 Oct 2026 in the staged reader at 1100, 768, 543 and 375 px: lessons 1 to 5 have 257, 380, 295, 666 and 414 formulas, 0 rendering errors, 0 wide formulas, no sideways page scroll. After the first measurement 65 formulas were stacked or moved into the text (displays with equation tags lost the tag and are named in the text), after the second 1.

open_obligations: The theorem is proved for all n >= n_0 with an n_0 that the lessons do not compute. With the constants of the lessons the last comparison needs log n >= 3401; the other conditions on n are far weaker but are only stated as 'for large n' (they were tested numerically at n = 10^10, 10^12 + 1 and 10^14).

Fields of positive characteristic: the bound for circuits (third lesson) holds over every field, but the lower bound for the rank measure of iterated matrix multiplication is proved over the complex numbers and transferred only to characteristic zero. Nothing is proved for positive characteristic.
Not in the course: the comparison with earlier lower bounds for bounded-depth circuits and the attributions in Section 1 and Section 3.1 of the manuscript; those papers were not read for this course.
The lessons were written and checked by one model in one session; they have not been checked by a second reader.
